name: wyrd-fence
description: wyrd-fence: path containment for one granted folder, read and create. A pre-existing hard link inside it still reaches outside. See the README section 'Security boundary and limits'.
//types: ⚠⚠ `types` POINTS AT THE FILE CARRYING THE SHAPES, NEVER AT A BARREL. `extractDeclarationApi` (this package's OWN `E12-declaration-inventory` arm — it was the Reader's until the 2026-09-01 relocation and now lives in `test/`, beside the surface it grades) parses top-level statements out of ONE `.d.ts`. A barrel of `export * from './fsgate.js'` yields a single re-export statement and NO shapes: E12 goes green against an empty extraction, and the documented recovery — `node scripts/declaration-baseline.mjs` — regenerates the baseline from that same empty extraction, after which the arm compares nothing against nothing and CAN NEVER FAIL AGAIN. Adding an index barrel here is therefore not a tidying change; it silently disarms the only guard on this package's public type surface.
//files: The build info sits inside `dist` so that deleting `dist` genuinely forces `tsc -b` to rebuild — a stale `.tsbuildinfo` beside a deleted output tree is how a build-mode compiler skips work it needed to do. It is negated here so it does not ship.
//scripts: ⚠ `mutate` BUILDS ONCE AND THEN DRIVES THE RUNNER DIRECTLY, NEVER `npm test`. `test` is `build && run-tests`, so a mutation loop routed through it would recompile `dist/` from `src/` and ERASE the dist-patched mutant before the suite saw it — every mutant then SURVIVES and reads as a weak guard rather than as a dead instrument. Three false survivors were measured that way on 2026-08-31. `scripts/mutate.mjs` builds once by hand (`npm run build && npm run mutate`) and drives `scripts/run-tests.mjs` DIRECTLY. ⚠ `declaration-baseline` is deliberately ABSENT from every automatic hook — it regenerates E12's oracle and a human runs it by name, having read the diff.
